title: Andre, 31: The 84-Month Car Loan Trap

scenes.say: $11,250. That's the interest on Andre's new car.
He borrowed $32,000 at about 9%, and picked 84 months.
Why? The payment looked small. About $515 a month.
But after 3 years, he still owes roughly $20,700.
Over 7 years, he pays back about $43,250 in total.
On 60 months, interest drops to about $7,850. That's $3,400 kept.
The fix: a cheaper car, a bigger down payment, or a shorter loan.

items.text: Look at total cost, not monthly

scenes.say: How long is your car loan? Subscribe so you don't make this mistake on your next paycheck, because $32,000 can cost $11,250 in interest.

description: Andre, 31, financed a $32,000 car at about 9% APR over 84 months. The roughly $515 payment looks easy, but he pays about $11,250 in interest — around $3,400 more than on a 60-month loan. Numbers are rounded US estimates and assume a fixed rate.
